FromSoftware Pushes The Duskbloods Release to 2027, Extending Development After Network Test Feedback

31 Oct 2026, 08:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Gaming Desk · Source: gamerant.com

Image: gamerant.com — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Official delay confirmed On **October 29, 2026**, FromSoftware announced that its upcoming Switch 2 exclusive, *The Duskbloods*, will now target a **2027** launch. The studio did not give a specific month or quarter, but said the title has entered its *"final adjustme

Official delay confirmed

On October 29, 2026, FromSoftware announced that its upcoming Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, will now target a 2027 launch. The studio did not give a specific month or quarter, but said the title has entered its "final adjustment stage" and will use the additional time to refine combat, strategic depth, and player expression based on recent player feedback.

Background and timeline

The Duskbloods was first revealed in April 2025 and, as of February 2026, was still listed for a 2026 release, though no exact date had ever been set. By late summer, fans noted the absence of a marketing push and began speculating about a delay. Those suspicions were confirmed when FromSoftware formally updated the schedule.

What the network test revealed

FromSoftware conducted a public network test over five sessions (August 21‑24, 2026). The test covered:

  • One of three planned maps
  • Six of ten launch characters
  • A subset of weapons, skills, Virtue rewards, and other equipment (all subject to change)

During the first session, widespread login problems forced an early shutdown. The remaining sessions proceeded, and a questionnaire remained open until September 4 for both participants and non‑participants. The studio said the test showed "particular player interest in the game's ‘combat, strategic depth, and player expression.’" At the same time, it identified technical and balance issues that will be addressed before launch.

Impact on Switch 2’s third‑party lineup

The delay removes one of the few high‑profile third‑party titles slated for the Switch 2 in 2026. The Duskbloods is notable for being a Nintendo‑exclusive project from FromSoftware, a departure from the studio’s recent multi‑platform releases such as Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Elden Ring, Armored Core 6: Fires of Rubicon, and the Elden Ring Nightreign multiplayer expansion. The exclusivity decision drew criticism when announced, and the postponement may deepen frustration among fans who were already disappointed by the lack of a broader platform release.

Practical implications for players

  • Pre‑order plans: With no concrete release window, retailers are unlikely to open pre‑orders until at least early 2027. Consumers should wait for an official announcement before committing funds.
  • Community expectations: The extended development window suggests FromSoftware is prioritising polish over a rushed launch. Players can anticipate more refined combat mechanics and balanced systems compared with earlier builds.
  • Competitive landscape: The Switch 2’s library will rely more heavily on first‑party titles and other exclusives for 2026. Gamers looking for new third‑party experiences may need to turn to PlayStation, Xbox, or PC platforms until The Duskbloods arrives.

How to verify the announcement

The delay was communicated through FromSoftware’s official channels on October 29, 2026. The full statement and details of the network test are available on the original article hosted by GameRant: [https://gamerant.com/duskbloods-switch-2-release-date-delay-2027/](https://gamerant.com/duskbloods-switch-2-release-date-delay-2027/) Readers can cross‑check the information by visiting FromSoftware’s newsroom or Nintendo’s press releases, which typically echo major schedule changes for exclusive titles.

Outlook

While the postponement pushes The Duskbloods out of the immediate 2026 window, FromSoftware’s commitment to addressing player feedback may result in a more polished experience at launch. The decision also underscores the challenges of developing a major third‑party title for a new console generation, especially when technical issues arise during early network testing. Until a narrower release window is announced, the gaming community will continue to monitor official channels for updates.
